record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.context_brief: Coanalytic separators of WF and UB
record.original_question: Let WF be the set of well-founded trees on ω and UB the set of trees on ω having a unique infinite branch. Saint Raymond proved that (WF, UB) is a coanalytic complete pair by descriptive-set-theoretic methods, and Goh proved using recursion theory that every coanalytic separator of WF and UB is coanalytic complete, which also yields Saint Raymond's theorem. Can the latter result be proved using descriptive-set-theoretic methods instead of recursion theory?

evidence.quote: Recall that WF is the collection of all well-founded trees on ω and UB is the collection of all trees on ω which have a unique infinite branch.

Using recursion theory, Goh proved that any coanalytic separator of WF and UB is coanalytic complete. The method also proves Saint Raymond’s theorem. Problem 5. Can this be proved using Descriptive Set Theoretic methods?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the Polish space of trees on ω (subsets of ω^{<ω} closed under taking initial segments, identified with elements of 2^{ω^{<ω}}). Let
  WF = { T : T is a well-founded tree on ω } (i.e., T has no infinite branch),
  UB = { T : T has a unique infinite branch }.
Both WF and UB are coanalytic (Π¹₁) subsets of the space of trees, and they are disjoint.

A coanalytic separator of WF and UB is a coanalytic set S ⊆ 2^{ω^{<ω}} with WF ⊆ S and S ∩ UB = ∅.

A coanalytic set C in a Polish space X is called coanalytic complete (Π¹₁-complete) if for every coanalytic set A in a Polish space Y there is a continuous function f : Y → X with A = f^{-1}(C). A pair (A₀, A₁) of disjoint coanalytic subsets of a Polish space X is called a coanalytic complete pair if for every pair (B₀, B₁) of disjoint coanalytic subsets of a Polish space Y there is a continuous function f : Y → X such that B₀ = f^{-1}(A₀) and B₁ = f^{-1}(A₁).

It is known that (WF, UB) is a coanalytic complete pair, and that every coanalytic separator S of WF and UB is itself coanalytic complete; the latter implies the former.

Problem. Provide a proof, using only descriptive-set-theoretic methods (without invoking recursion theory), that every coanalytic separator S of WF and UB is coanalytic complete.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a 2025 compilation of open problems in computability theory and descriptive set theory. No subsequent paper providing a purely descriptive-set-theoretic proof was located.
